svg.title: The slice loop
svg.desc: Flowchart of seven sequential steps for one unit of work — design, agree, red, green, review, human gate, as-built reconciliation. An objection at step 2 opens a bounded adjudication exchange, shown as a five-rung ladder that ends rather than cycling: the adjudicator replies before it edits with one verdict per objection, AGREE or DISAGREE, stating any change it would make without making it; the finding and the proposed remedy are judged separately, so accepting a real problem while rejecting or narrowing its fix is a legitimate outcome; the objector may answer once; if the two still disagree the architect may call a vote from a third role that owns neither side, whose reasoned verdict is advisory to the architect on architecture and to the human on scope and is recorded either way; and only then is the design amended, in one pass, with the rulings attached. Separately, any role at any step — 2, 3 and 4 as well as 5 — may raise a design change request, which blocks the slice for one round of discussion with four possible outcomes: a clarification resumes from the raising step, a deferred improvement merges as-is and spawns a backlog slice plus a proposed ADR, defer-to-the-gate is ruled now and reviewed by the human at step 6, and a design defect returns to step 1 — the only outcome drawn as a return path, and one the architect may rule only by naming the acceptance criterion, quality scenario or standing invariant that would fail, at most twice per slice before the slice auto-escalates.
svg.text: ANY ROLE MAY RAISE A DCR
NON-NEGOTIABLE · ONE ROUND, THEN A DECISION
REPLY BEFORE YOU EDIT — one verdict per objection,
AGREE or DISAGREE, reasoning stated. Where it agrees
it states the change it would make; it does not make it.
FINDING AND REMEDY ARE JUDGED SEPARATELY — a real
problem with the wrong fix is a legitimate outcome.
STILL APART — THE ARCHITECT MAY CALL A VOTE: a third
role owning neither side returns a reasoned verdict,
advisory to architect or human, recorded either way.
THE ROUND ENDS HERE — NO SECOND EXCHANGE
ONLY THEN IS THE DESIGN AMENDED — in one pass,
Raised at any step, by any role
SLICE BLOCKED · ONE ROUND · FOUR OUTCOMES
back to step 1 · supersede the ADR · revise
architect rules now · the gate reviews it
TO RULE (c) THE ARCHITECT MUST NAME THE ACCEPTANCE
CRITERION, QS-* OR §2 INVARIANT THAT WOULD FAIL —
IF IT CANNOT NAME ONE, THE OUTCOME IS (b).
costs a cycle and a loopback
Loopback — only outcome (c), max 2 per slice, then escalate
